ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory continuous screening of all direct and indirect shareholders, UBOs, statutory signatories and beneficiary payment accounts against: (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (ii) the EU Consolidated Sanctions List (Council Regulation (EU) No. 269/2010, No. 833/2014 as amended, and No. 2580/2001); (iii) the OFAC SDN List given the USD-denominated settlement flows of Apple IAP and Google Play Billing; and (iv) TRACFIN national targeted files. PEP classification and enhanced due diligence are mandated by Articles L. 561-10 I-2° and R. 561-20-2 of the French Monetary and Financial Code and 5AMLD, with senior-management approval and ongoing transaction monitoring whenever a PEP is identified, irrespective of country of residence. Any discrepancy in a UBO declaration must be reported to TRACFIN within the statutory deadlines.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) via the Guichet unique portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); name availability screening performed through Infogreffe and the INPI trademark database
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The dénomination sociale must be expressed in Latin script and readable in French legal records (Articles L. 227-1 and R. 123-44 of the French Commercial Code; Article 1835 of the Civil Code). Foreign-language or non-Latin names must be transliterated into Latin characters and may coexist with the original script only as a secondary identifier. The name must not create confusion with an existing registered company or trademark in the competent territorial jurisdiction. Every commercial instrument and the Kbis must bear the name followed or preceded by 'SAS' or 'Société par Actions Simplifiée', together with the share capital amount.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: France (where it implies official state sponsorship and requires prior authorization)
Europe (where it implies official EU patronage)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France operates no formal pre-reservation system: the proposed name is validated only upon incorporation filing before the greffe du tribunal de commerce, which rules within approximately 5 working days. The RNE entry becomes final and the name is then protected against subsequent conflicting registrations. If the greffe rejects the name on distinctiveness or public-order grounds, the applicant may file a reasoned administrative challenge before the judge responsible for supervision of the commercial and companies register (juge chargé de la surveillance du registre du commerce et des sociétés) of the competent tribunal de commerce, or seek interim relief (référé). The applicant may alternatively submit a corrective filing through the RNE Guichet unique with an amended distinctive element, without forfeiting the underlying application fees. A refusal may also be contested before the INPI's administrative review channel where the decision is attributable to the RNE data-processing service.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible subject to prior approval. The SAS must maintain a genuine physical seat in France under Articles L. 210-1 and L. 123-11-1 of the French Commercial Code, whether through ownership, a lease, a co-working desk contract, or a domiciliation agreement with a préfecture-approved domiciliation provider (Article R. 123-166). A pure virtual mailbox without an approved domiciliation firm is rejected by the greffe. For the Digital Webtoon Publishing industry, approved domiciliation is acceptable for the entire corporate lifetime, but Apple IAP and Google Play Billing merchant onboarding and French VAT registration under Article 289 of the French General Tax Code (CGI) require a verifiable correspondence address matching the Kbis public record.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified annual risk for a Low_Risk_Standard digital publishing profile: <5% probability of an unannounced inspection by the greffe, police fiscale or TRACFIN within the first 36 months; 100% probability of a yearly physical verification by the licensed domiciliation provider; 15-20% probability of supplementary on-site or video-audited documentation checks by acquiring banks or Apple/Google payment verification teams before the first EUR payout is released.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); national portals: www.impots.gouv.fr (professional e-services Espace Professionnel), www.formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises, single business-registration gateway), and www.impots.gouv.fr/oss (EU One Stop Shop for VOlT and distance sales). Non-resident operators are handled by the DGFiP Service des Impôts des Entreprises étrangères (SIE étranger) in Paris.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1: French-incorporated SAS obtains SIREN/SIRET automatically from INSEE via the Guichet Unique after corporate registration; STEP 2: DGFiP issues the intra-EU VAT identification number (FRTVAnnnnnnnnn based on the SIREN) and activates the corporate income tax (IS) and VAT accounts under the same SIREN fiscal file; STEP 3: foreign entities without a French establishment that cannot use reverse charge or OSS must file DGFiP Form 15771-SD with the SIE étranger, appointing a DGFiP-approved fiscal representative (représentant fiscal agréé) when established outside the EU and potentially posting a bank guarantee; STEP 4: a French business bank account and a gestion mandate or power of attorney are practical prerequisites; STEP 5: processing time is typically 5–10 days for French incorporations and 2 weeks to 2 months for non-resident direct VAT registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope (Pass_Through_Eligible only via temporary statutory election). An SAS is by default a separate legal person subject to corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS) under CGI Art. 206-1, with no fiscal transparency in the standard regime; IS is levied at 25% with a reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of annual profit for qualifying SMEs (Turnover below EUR 10,000,000; 75%+ individual ownership); French territoriality (CGI Art. 209-I) confines IS to profits derived from activities carried on in France, save for any ministerial-approved worldwide or consolidated election. For VAT, the SAS is an entity-level taxable person and its French head-office registration covers all French establishments.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: CGI Art. 239 bis AB: a qualifying small SAS (Turnover below EUR 10,000,000, majority held by individuals with substance, unlisted) may elect, for a maximum of five fiscal years, to be fiscally transparent and taxed at the shareholder level under Impôt sur le Revenu (IR); CGI Art. 223 A: a French parent holding at least 95% of a subsidiary may elect the tax-integrated group regime (intégration fiscale) for consolidated IS; CGI Art. 209: ministerial approval may be obtained for worldwide profits (bénéfice mondial) or consolidated (bénéfice consolidé) taxation. France has no US-style check-the-box election and no elective hybrid-mismatch treatment: ATAD anti-hybrid rules (CGI Arts. 7, 12 and 209-0 A et seq.) apply automatically. For indirect tax, an EU-established SAS may elect the OSS (One Stop Shop) regime to declare EU-wide B2C e-services from France and may drop out of the French micro-enterprise VAT franchise.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA), harmonized under EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC and implemented by CGI Arts. 256 et seq.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France has no general VAT registration threshold for an incorporated SAS; the micro-enterprise exemption (franchise en base de TVA) applies only below EUR 36,800 of annual turnover for services and EUR 91,900 for goods (prestations de services and ventes thresholds, annually adjusted; upper ranges EUR 44,300 and EUR 101,000). A commercial webtoon publishing operation monetized via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing will normally exceed these limits, so the SAS must register and charge French VAT from the first euro on domestic B2C electronic supplies. For intra-EU cross-border B2C digital services (Chapter unlocking, subscriptions), the pan-EU annual threshold of EUR 10,000 (CGI Art. 293 A ter) triggers OSS registration and VAT accounting in each member state of consumption; non-established foreign digital suppliers must collect French VAT with no de minimis threshold on French consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is deploying a transaction-based e-invoicing and e-reporting reform: from 1 September 2026 large and mid-size enterprises must issue structured e-invoices (FACTUR-X, UBL) for B2B supplies through a certified Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP) or the public portal Chorus Pro (PPF); small and micro enterprises join on 1 September 2027 (loi de finances 2023 and décret n° 2024-219). B2C payment and transaction data (e-reporting) for both domestic and cross-border flows are transmitted to DGFiP by the PDP/PPF in periodic batch files; there is no real-time per-invoice fiscal clearance and no digital stamping akin to the Italian SDI or Turkish regimes, but certified PDPs expose APIs consistent with the national Chorus Pro/NITVAN e-invoicing specifications. B2G e-invoicing on Chorus Pro has been mandatory since 2017. For app-store digital distribution, Apple and Google may be deemed suppliers of the B2C supply under the EU e-commerce VAT package (Art. 9a of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1315), meaning the French SAS must keep OSS listings, reverse-charge evidence and platform settlement statements in lieu of classic invoice flow.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of physical goods outside the EU qualify for French VAT zero-rating (exonération) under CGI Art. 262-I, and intra-Community supplies of goods to EU VAT-registered customers qualify under CGI Art. 261 C-I, provided the exporter retains proof that the goods physically left the French or EU territory; services directly connected to export transport and handling are likewise zero-rated under CGI Art. 262-II. For the actual webtoon digital-publishing model, 'export zero-rating' is largely inapplicable: B2B licenses and cross-border syndication contracts are taxed in the customer's country under the general place-of-supply rule (CGI Arts. 258, 259, 259 A), with the French supplier issuing a reverse-charge invoice without French VAT and quoting the customer's valid EU VAT ID; B2C digital services to foreign consumers are statutorily taxable only in the consumer's country (CGI Art. 259 D), which produces de facto 0% French taxation. Claims of 0% on any physical deluxe/print export must be matched by shipping evidence and the remittance of export consideration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAE / DAU - EX-E) lodged via DELTA-X with the exporter-of-record status matching the SAS EORI number (FR...)
Bill of Lading / CMR / airway bill evidencing physical departure of the goods from EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT confirmation evidencing settlement of export proceeds by the foreign customer
Commercial invoice addressed to the foreign importer with Incoterms and export terms
Packing list (applicable to physical deluxe reprints, collectibles or printed webtoon volumes)
Proof of intra-Community supply: customer's valid EU VAT ID and the recapitulative statement entry for EU zero-rated dispatches
International syndication or licensing agreement evidencing the offshore digital-service B2B transaction
For the app-store channel only: Apple/Google settlement statements and OSS country-by-country listings in substitution for customs documentation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP's recovery right generally runs until the end of the third calendar year following the year the VAT became chargeable (CGI Livre des procédures fiscales, Art. L169); the window extends to ten years where the zero-rating claim is tainted by occult activity or fraudulent maneuvers (Art. L176 LPF). If audit evidence shows goods never left France, forged export proofs, artificial delay in repatriating exports proceeds without economic justification (abus de droit under Art. L64 LPF), or digital supplies mislabeled as exports, DGFiP retroactively reclassifies the receipts as French-standard-rated supplies at 20%, claws back the VAT, applies late-payment interest (intérêt de retard at 0.20% per month), and triggers penalties under CGI Art. 1729: 40% increase for bad faith (mauvaise foi) or 80% for fraudulent maneuvers (manœuvres frauduleuses), alongside 10% for ordinary filing negligence. Criminal exposure under CGI Art. 1741 reaches EUR 500,000 fine and 5 years' imprisonment, elevated to EUR 750,000 and 7 years for organized fraud; directors and de facto managers may be held solidarity liable, and the customer's input-credit claim is denied when the export/zero-rating evidence fails the legal documentation tests (CGI Annex II, Art. 271).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France; foreign exchange regulatory competence shared with the Direction Générale du Trésor and the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies full current and capital account convertibility of the euro. No prior exchange-control license is required for current payments, capital movements, dividends, or profit repatriation under EU Treaty freedoms and the French Monetary and Financial Code. The only mandatory formality is statistical balance-of-payments (BOP) declaration to Banque de France when capital or direct investment flows exceed certain reporting thresholds; profit remittance requires duly approved annual accounts, a formal board/shareholder distribution resolution, and standard AML/KYC checks, but no FX conversion permit.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory foreign-currency conversion ratio or timeline. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency, used directly for current payments, or converted to euros at the exporter's discretion; however, all correspondent transactions remain subject to EU/UN sanctions screening and French AML/CFT due diligence.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. An EU/EEA-licensed electronic money institution (EMI) can passport into France under PSD2 and may accept euro balances; however, an EMI is not a full credit institution, cannot offer commercial credit, and must safeguard client funds with a credit institution. Non-EU fintechs require ACPR registration or a French branch, and digital-content subscription flows can trigger enhanced AML requirements; therefore an EMI is viable as a collection and disbursement rail but should be supplemented by a tier-1 bank for capital escrow, clearing, and derivative execution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not uniformly require all directors to appear physically; but the AML/CFT customer due diligence standard under the Monetary and Financial Code demands reliable identity verification, and remote opening is generally accepted for EU/EEA nationals using a qualified eIDAS-compliant video identity solution. For non-resident or non-EU directors, the bank de facto requires certified true copies (apostille/certified translation) of passports, proof of address, corporate extracts, and often an in-person or video interview. Physical presence at the bank or in front of a French notary remains the safest approach for first-time onboarding and any high-risk indicator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders or indirect beneficial owners sprinkled through multi-tier entities, trusts, or nominee arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO register (register des bénéficiaires effectifs) and corporate org chart; SAS articles and shareholders’ agreements; apostilled/certified translations of foreign registry extracts; notarized source-of-wealth statement; tax residence certificates; audited financial statements or accountant letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP (politically exposed person) status, sanctions-list screening hits, or counterparties in high-risk/AML-deficient jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence questionnaire; PEP status declaration by each beneficial owner; legitimate commercial-reason memorandum; independent sanctions/OFAC/FATF screening report; bank reference from the originating bank; contracts with Apple/Google/distributors; copy of public IP registration (e.g. copyright assignments) evidencing real business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear economic purpose or inconsistent flows of subscription revenues and royalty out-payments through the banking account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform payout reports from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing; webtoon license and syndication contracts with detailed royalty calculation; subscriber/chapter-unlocking analytics; explanation of refunds; accountant’s letter confirming alignment between accounting entries and bank flows; VAT status and French anti-fraud declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or unstructured inbound capital injection requiring plausible source of funds and wealth creation pathway.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital increase resolution and signed subscription form; issuance and registration recepissé (K-bis or legalization publication); source-of-funds documentation (bank statements, sale agreement, inheritance/tax documents); founding shareholders’ biographical statements; prior-year tax returns; notarized certificate for non-cash contributions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Required routing is a SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder’s bank to the French SAS’s euro current/escrow account (FR76 IBAN), or a SEPA Credit Transfer for EU/EEA funds. For statistical purposes, remittance information must indicate the economic nature, e.g. “SHARE CAPITAL INCREASE / SUBSCRIPTION” (and, where applicable, a Banque de France BOP transaction code), and the bank will classify the payment internally. The SAS must produce the capital increase resolution, K-bis filing, UBO declaration, source of funds documentation, and confirm the absence of sanctions exposure. Funds cannot be drawn for operating purposes before completion of legal capital formation formalities if held in a dedicated escrow account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound clearing rails are: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer / SEPA Instant for euro royalties and chapter revenue shares to EU/EEA creators; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for non-EU creators, foreign distributors, and profit-sharing payments; (iii) commercial documentary letters of credit for structured payments linked to physical collateral or complex IP trade terms; and (iv) intra-group settlement through TARGET2 via the French bank. All messages require beneficiary IBAN/BIC (or correspondent BIC for non-IBAN countries), economic purpose text, reference to the underlying license/royalty agreement, and withholding tax forms where royalties cross borders.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot transactions for same-day/next-day conversion of foreign-currency subscription receipts into euros
Outright deliverable FX forwards (standard FXA contracts) for receivables and licence fees maturing within 12 months
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies not freely deliverable in the EU, settled in euro
FX/cross-currency swaps for structural alignment of foreign-currency revenue streams and disbursement peaks
Plain vanilla FX options (call/put) for asymmetric cover, subject to ISDA/CSA documentation and EMIR reporting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels: balance sheet, income statement, annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, filed through INPI Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after fiscal year-end; accounts must be approved by shareholders within 6 months of year-end, then filed within 1 month of approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to €1,500 for a legal entity under the French Commercial Code; the public prosecutor may order the company to file, and after formal notices the company may be struck off the register or subjected to a judicial injunction (astreinte)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner (UBO) re-confirmation incorporated in the annual renewal declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); filed via INPI Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the same 1 January - 31 March confirmation window; material changes in beneficial ownership must be declared within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-declaration or false declaration exposes the legal entity to a fine up to €15,000 under the Monetary and Financial Code; repeated omissions may also lead to RCS strike-off and inability to obtain a certificate of good standing (Kbis)

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit (Commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for a SAS when, at fiscal year-end, two of the following three thresholds are exceeded: balance sheet total €4,000,000; net turnover excluding tax €8,000,000; average workforce 50 employees. Additional triggers include holding/controlling subsidiaries requiring audit and requests by shareholders holding at least 10% of capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Code de commerce, Plan comptable général, ANC regulations); IFRS is optional at the individual level and mandatory for consolidated financial statements of listed groups only.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: During each annual RCS confirmation window, the SAS must reconfirm the identity of all ultimate beneficial owners (any individual directly or indirectly holding more than 25% of capital or voting rights, or exercising control). If shareholding transfers or control changes occur, a modification declaration must be filed within 30 days; the annual re-confirmation validates the continuing accuracy of the register on file with the registry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of share transfers and shareholders (registre des mouvements de titres), maintained at the registered office
Register of shareholder decisions and written consultations (registre des décisions de l'associé unique / assemblées), maintained at the registered office
Minute book/register of proceedings of the SAS governing bodies, including decisions of the President and General Management, maintained at the registered office

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$300-US$900 per annum for professional domiciliation, registered-office address and corporate secretarial support in a French business centre
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,500-US$12,000 per audit for a small-to-mid-size digital publishing SAS, depending on revenue complexity, digital platform sales through Apple/Google, and intercompany transactions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small and medium-sized companies may obtain a 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit if annual turnover does not exceed EUR 10 million, capital is fully paid, and at least 75% of the share capital and voting rights are held by individuals or qualifying entities. A 3.3% social contribution applies to companies with annual turnover of at least EUR 7.63 million and corporate income tax liability exceeding EUR 763,000, subject to statutory conditions. Research and development expenditure may qualify for a tax credit generally equal to 30% of eligible expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that amount. The French loss carryforward rule is legally unlimited, but utilization is generally capped at EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million in the relevant year; the supplied standardized field value of 5 years is not the current French statutory expiry period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD for the corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the French Tax Administration professional portal at impots.gouv.fr via the espace professionnel. Supporting corporate tax schedules generally include Forms 2058-A-SD, 2058-B-SD, 2058-C-SD and 2059 series, depending on the accounting regime.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return, with corporate income tax installments generally paid quarterly.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is generally due by the second working day after 1 May of the following year. For a financial year ending on a date other than 31 December, the return is generally due within three months after the financial year-end, subject to electronic filing calendar rules. Corporate income tax installments are generally due on 15 February, 15 May, 15 August and 15 November, with a final balance generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, French tax identification number, registered office, financial year dates, legal form, and tax office jurisdiction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the French SAS legal entity and French registered office. Record the foreign parent separately as shareholder or related party; do not use the parent company's tax identity as the SAS taxpayer identity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result before and after French tax adjustments, including accounting-to-tax reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only the SAS's French taxable result. Deductible expenses must be business-related, documented, properly accrued, and consistent with French transfer-pricing and anti-abuse rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2058-A-SD, accounting result to taxable result reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary add-backs, deductions, non-deductible expenses, depreciation adjustments, provisions, and tax-exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible taxes, penalties, excessive remuneration, unsupported provisions, non-business expenses, and expenses failing French deductibility requirements. Reconcile foreign-currency transactions using appropriate accounting records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Losses carried forward or carried back and losses utilized in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only losses legally attributable to the SAS. Current-year utilization is subject to the EUR 1 million plus 50% excess-profit limitation. Changes in activity or ownership may restrict preservation of tax losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2058-C-SD, tax credits and special deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, exemptions, special deductions, and other taxable-income adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits supported by contemporaneous evidence, including eligible R&D records, payroll data, invoices, and statutory declarations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital gains, depreciable assets, provisions, and other balance-sheet tax information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose relevant disposals, intellectual property transactions, and asset transfers at arm's length value. Cross-border transfers may trigger French exit-tax or valuation issues depending on the asset and transaction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax installment payment schedule and payment references.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay through the professional tax account. Monitor installment reductions carefully; underpayments may generate late-payment interest and penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax balance payment and refundable-credit position.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the final liability with installments, tax credits, withholding credits, and any group tax-consolidation position before payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual simplified transfer-pricing declaration for qualifying companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File where the applicable EUR 50 million turnover or gross-assets threshold and other statutory conditions are met. Ensure consistency with intercompany agreements, Local File, Master File and accounting ledgers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Separate VAT returns, EU sales lists, OSS/IOSS filings where applicable, and platform-related reporting.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Digital webtoon subscriptions, chapter unlocks and in-app sales require transaction-by-transaction VAT analysis, including customer location, platform principal-versus-agent status, consumer evidence and OSS treatment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted tax returns generally attract a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% for deliberate non-compliance and 80% for fraudulent maneuvers or abusive concealment. Late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Failure to use mandatory electronic filing or payment may trigger a 0.2% penalty, generally subject to a EUR 60 minimum where applicable. Tax reassessments may also include interest, penalties, withholding-tax assessments and director-liability proceedings.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Dividends paid by a French company to a non-resident corporate shareholder are generally subject to 25% French withholding tax, subject to domestic exemptions, EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, treaty relief and anti-abuse conditions. Dividends paid to non-resident individuals are generally subject to 12.8% withholding tax, subject to applicable rules and treaty treatment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The recipient should establish tax residence and beneficial ownership, satisfy limitation-on-benefits, principal-purpose, anti-abuse and minimum-holding requirements where relevant, and provide the applicable French tax-residence forms, generally Form 5000 and, for dividends, Form 5001. Relief may be applied at source when documentation is available and accepted; otherwise the payer withholds and the recipient files for a refund. EU Parent-Subsidiary relief generally requires qualifying EU ownership, a minimum 10% holding, minimum holding-period conditions, subject-to-tax requirements and absence of an artificial arrangement. Dividend distributions must also comply with French corporate-law distributable-profit and solvency requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and similar payments to non-residents are generally subject to French withholding tax at 25% under domestic law, subject to treaty limitation, EU rules and statutory exemptions. Ordinary interest paid to non-residents is generally not subject to French withholding tax under domestic law, except for specific anti-abuse, non-cooperative-jurisdiction or specially regulated situations; payments to certain non-cooperative jurisdictions may be subject to a 75% rate. Tax treaties commonly reduce royalty withholding to approximately 0% to 10% and interest withholding to approximately 0% to 15%, but the applicable rate depends on the recipient's residence, beneficial ownership and treaty article. Arm's-length pricing, treaty entitlement and substance must be documented.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory comprehensive Local File and Master File obligations generally apply where the French entity's annual turnover or gross assets are at least EUR 150 million, where it controls or is controlled by an entity meeting the statutory threshold, or where it belongs to a qualifying group containing an entity meeting the threshold. A Country-by-Country Report generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 750 million. An annual simplified transfer-pricing declaration generally applies at the EUR 50 million turnover or gross-assets threshold, subject to statutory conditions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no separate general Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to certain offshore ESR regimes. Substance remains required under French anti-abuse law, beneficial-ownership principles, treaty principal-purpose testing, EU anti-hybrid and anti-tax-avoidance rules, controlled-foreign-company rules, interest-limitation rules and the abuse-of-law doctrine. The SAS should maintain French decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or operational infrastructure, accounting records, bank control, commercial risk assumption and evidence of services actually received. A conduit company with no genuine functions, assets or risks may lose treaty benefits and face recharacterization, denied deductions, withholding assessments and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing revenue from digital subscriptions, in-app purchases, advertising, licensing or merchandise; maintaining false books; using undeclared bank accounts; or submitting materially false tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative reassessment, 40% penalty for deliberate failure or 80% penalty for fraudulent maneuvers, plus 0.20% monthly late-payment interest. Criminal tax fraud may result in up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine, increased in aggravated cases to up to seven years' imprisonment and EUR 3 million, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal prosecution and, under French Tax Procedure Code Article L267, personal joint liability for tax debts where fraudulent maneuvers or serious and repeated non-compliance made collection impossible. Civil restitution, asset seizure and professional disqualification may follow. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may be imposed or arise through judicial measures or tax-enforcement procedures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to charge or remit VAT on French or EU consumer sales, misclassifying B2C sales as B2B, omitting customer-location evidence, misusing OSS/IOSS, or incorrectly treating Apple or Google as principal rather than payment intermediary or merchant of record.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, late-payment interest, 10% to 80% penalties depending on conduct, potential criminal tax-fraud exposure, and loss of VAT registration or platform compliance privileges where applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur liability for intentional or grossly negligent VAT misconduct, including tax-debt recovery actions, criminal penalties and disqualification. Personal liability is fact-dependent and is not automatic merely because the company failed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length royalties, management fees, content-acquisition fees, financing costs or commission payments to foreign affiliates; shifting webtoon intellectual property without valuation support; or using a zero-profit French distributor without functional justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable profit, denial of deductions, withholding-tax reassessment, 40% or 80% penalties where applicable, documentation penalties, and possible Article 57 French tax-adjustment proceedings. The absence of a Local File or Master File can trigger a specific documentation fine calculated under statutory rules, potentially reaching the greater of a fixed statutory minimum or 0.5% of the amount covered by undocumented transactions, subject to applicable caps and amendments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed where they approved fraudulent arrangements, concealed related-party transactions or caused serious and repeated tax non-compliance. Ordinary pricing disputes do not automatically create personal criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, royalties or interest through an entity lacking personnel, functions, assets, decision-making or commercial risk, with the principal purpose of obtaining reduced treaty withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or EU relief, withholding-tax assessment at domestic rates, interest, anti-abuse penalties, abuse-of-law recharacterization and possible criminal tax-fraud exposure where concealment or falsification is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal liability for knowingly implementing sham structures, together with asset seizure and personal tax-debt recovery in aggravated cases. Treaty relief is denied based on facts; corporate limited liability is not automatically disregarded.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared beneficial ownership and corporate transparency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify or update the ultimate beneficial owner of the SAS, filing inaccurate ownership information, concealing nominee arrangements or using layered entities to obscure control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil and criminal sanctions may include fines, injunctions, restrictions on registration or access to corporate services, and related anti-money-laundering measures. False declarations may constitute a separate criminal offense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives and beneficial owners may face personal criminal exposure for intentional false declarations or obstruction. Directors may also face disqualification and asset-seizure measures where linked to money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting proceeds from piracy, counterfeit merchandise, sanctioned persons, fraud, ransomware, undisclosed cryptocurrency activity or unexplained third-party payment flows; or failing to maintain risk-based customer and payment controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering may result in up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine, with aggravated sanctions potentially reaching ten years' imprisonment and EUR 750,000 or more under applicable circumstances. Confiscation, account freezing and regulatory reporting measures may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be prosecuted personally for intentional participation, facilitation or negligent governance where legally applicable. Courts may impose imprisonment, fines, confiscation, disqualification and judicial supervision; travel restrictions may be ordered in criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Copyright, licensing and unauthorized content exploitation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Syndicating webtoon chapters without valid territorial rights, exceeding licensed language or platform scope, failing to pay contractual royalties, or using AI-generated or translated content without rights clearance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Injunctions, withdrawal or blocking orders, damages, restitution of profits, seizure of infringing materials and criminal copyright penalties. Copyright infringement may generally attract up to three years' imprisonment and a EUR 300,000 fine, with increased sanctions for organized or aggravated conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal exposure for knowing infringement or organized infringement and may be liable for civil restitution where they personally participated or abused the corporate form. Ordinary corporate infringement does not automatically pierce the SAS liability shield.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper dividend distribution and unlawful profit repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable profit, distributing capital in breach of creditor-protection rules, paying dividends while the company is insolvent, or remitting funds as sham royalties, loans or service fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of unlawful dividends, corporate-law sanctions, tax reassessment, withholding-tax liability, interest and penalties. Fraudulent insolvency conduct may trigger additional criminal and civil sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be required to restore assets, compensate creditors, bear liability for management faults contributing to an insufficient asset position and face disqualification or criminal prosecution. Shareholders receiving dividends in bad faith may also face repayment claims.
